text:
release-manager: Quick alert — payment-service v3.4.2 canary failed during the 19:00 change window. Deploybot stopped promotion. We need a fast decision: retag+republish, pin to last-known-good, or abort migration? :rotating_light:

deploybot: PROMOTION HALT: IMAGE_ATTEST_TTL Drift. Release manifest expects attestation timestamp within 30s of build; observed attestation in gcr-us is older. Registry digest mismatch observed: release-manifest: sha256:1111aaaa2222, gcr-us observed: sha256:3333bbbb4444. Code: ERR_IMAGE_ATTEST_TTL

ci-bot: Build 2024-09-14T18:45:00Z created multi-arch manifest. Attestation signed with CI KMS key but timestamp skewed due to delayed signing job (we retried signing at 18:46:50). Mirror to eu-west likely read prior manifest during replicate window.

anya: @release-manager I can re-run the publish pipeline to re-sign and re-push, but that will create new manifest digest and require a new release manifest bump. That will also invalidate the current rollout ID. Thoughts on risk tolerance?

josh: Migration included a schema update that backfills a non-critical index. If we push a new digest mid-window we'll lose traceability for this rollout id. Safer to pin to the last-known-good digest and schedule republish after window.

sasha: Infra note — GCR regional mirrors have a known 60-120s read-after-write anomaly when cache TTLs align badly with replication. We need to check cosign/KMS annotation consistency before forcing a re-publish; otherwise we risk attestation orphaning.

release-manager: Product and legal want a clean audit trail. Pinning preserves auditability because we point to a previously attested digest. Republish will require new attestation and new release notes. Proposal: pin to v3.4.1@sha256:aaaa1111dead to abort migration, then investigate signing latency and mirror behavior.

phil-oncall: I can perform the pin and coordinate with deploybot. Pin procedure: update k8s image to pinned digest and run deploybot promote. Command example provided by deploybot below. I'll watch logs for any sidecars that might pick the stale digest. ETA ~12m.

deploybot: To pin now, run:
```
# set deployment to known-good digest
kubectl set image deploy/payment-service payment-service=gcr.io/redwood-prod/payment-service@sha256:aaaa1111dead --namespace=prod
# trigger manual promotion
/deploy promote payment-service --from-manual
```
Note: deploybot will still reject any manifest if attestation annotations don't match the release manifest.

mia: From PM — prefer pin+hold. Please add release-note: "Migration paused; investigating registry attest timestamp drift. No customer risk currently." I can draft and post.

anya: Ok pin path seems lowest-risk. I'll hold off on republish until infra confirms cosign annotations line up. After pin I'll re-run the signing job in a staging loop to validate timestamp behavior.

josh: Agreed. Decision: pin to sha256:aaaa1111dead (v3.4.1) and abort v3.4.2 promotion. Debug signing and replication off-hours, then re-schedule migration in a later change window if safe.

release-manager: Action items: @anya hold republish, @phil-oncall perform pin + notify post-promotion, @mia write release note, @sasha open infra ticket with replication logs and cosign annotation diffs. I'll update the release board.

phil-oncall: Pinning now. Will post status in ~10m.

deploybot: Promotion event: payment-service pinned to gcr.io/redwood-prod/payment-service@sha256:aaaa1111dead. Rollout started at 1715090045.

phil-oncall: Rollout stable on 3 replicas in eu-west and us-central after 7m checks. No schema change applied. Holding release until infra ticket REG-3500 completes.

mia: Release note posted: "Hold: payment-service migration paused due to registry attestation timestamp drift. Teams investigating; rollout deferred." :pencil:

sasha: Created infra ticket REG-3500 with cosign annotation snapshots and mirror timestamps, assigned to registry-team.

release-manager: Thanks team. We'll reconvene once REG-3500 has updates. Closing thread for this change window. :lock:
